text:
sara: Hey team — quick question. I'm planning to go on unpaid medical leave next month for IVF treatments. Two things: 1) Can I still submit HSA receipts for reimbursement while I'm on unpaid leave? 2) I have a 401(k) loan with payroll deductions — will the pause in payroll break the loan payments or cause a default? @priya any guidance?

priya (people-ops): hi @sara :wave: sorry to hear — quick answers up front: HSA reimbursements for qualified expenses are generally allowed even if you're on unpaid leave, as long as the HSA account exists and expenses were incurred after you were eligible. For the 401(k) loan, payroll deductions are the usual mechanism; an unpaid-payroll period can cause missed payments unless we arrange an alternative.

ben (payroll): tagging in from payroll. Two practical options:
- We can set up an off-cycle ACH repayment so you continue loan payments while on leave. We'll need signed authorization and the amount/schedule.
- Alternatively, you can make manual payments to the plan administrator. Note: if a payment is missed and not cured within the plan's cure period, it could be treated as a distribution (taxable + 10% penalty if under 59½).

priya (people-ops): Steps to move forward:
1) For HSA: submit claims through the benefits portal (link: https://benefits.redwood.example/claims) or email benefits@redwood.com with receipts and dates of service. We can reimburse from the HSA even if payroll contributions pause.
2) For 401(k) loan: reply here or DM Ben with preferred repayment option (ACH off-cycle or manual). If you want ACH, Ben will send an authorization form. If you expect a long unpaid period, we can also discuss temporarily increasing post-leave payroll deductions to catch up, but that requires plan admin approval.

sara: thanks that's super helpful. For HSA, some receipts are for meds paid before leave starts and some during — both qualify?

priya (people-ops): as long as the expenses were incurred after you were HSA-eligible, timing relative to leave doesn't matter. So meds bought before leave but after eligibility are fine. Keep receipts and dates.

ben (payroll): @sara if you want ACH, say "ACH-yes" here and I'll DM the form. If you prefer manual payments, tell me how often you'll pay and we'll note it. Also FYI: if employment status changes (e.g., termination) there is a loan offset treatment — we can cover that if needed later.

people-ops-bot: Reminder added to benefits queue (#12345). Priya will follow up within 2 business days. :white_check_mark:

sara: ACH-yes please. I'll DM the bank details. Really appreciate the quick answers :heart:

priya (people-ops): got it — assigning to Ben for the ACH form and to benefits for HSA claims. LMK if you want us to loop in the plan admin for any catch-up payment arrangements.
